# `<util/pipe.h>`

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_docs.py in kagantmr/zuzu. Do not edit. -->

Pipes are a one way stream between spaces.

```c
#include <util/pipe.h>
```

## Constants

| Name | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| <a id="pipe_page_size"></a>`PIPE_PAGE_SIZE` | `4096u` | Page size the pipe layout is built on. |
| <a id="pipe_hdr_size"></a>`PIPE_HDR_SIZE` | `PIPE_PAGE_SIZE` | The header occupies page 0; the ring's data starts on page 1. |
| <a id="pipe_size_min"></a>`PIPE_SIZE_MIN` | `4096u` | Smallest ring: one data page. |
| <a id="pipe_size_default"></a>`PIPE_SIZE_DEFAULT` | `16384u` | Default ring for shell pipelines: four data pages, five pages in all. |
| <a id="pipe_size_max"></a>`PIPE_SIZE_MAX` | `262144u` | Largest ring. |
| <a id="pipe_default_data_bit"></a>`PIPE_DEFAULT_DATA_BIT` | `0u` | Event bit CreatePipe() uses for "bytes were written". |
| <a id="pipe_default_space_bit"></a>`PIPE_DEFAULT_SPACE_BIT` | `1u` | Event bit CreatePipe() uses for "bytes were read, there is room". |
| <a id="pipe_f_writer_closed"></a>`PIPE_F_WRITER_CLOSED` | `(1u << 0)` | The writer is gone. A reader sees EOF once the ring drains. |
| <a id="pipe_f_reader_closed"></a>`PIPE_F_READER_CLOSED` | `(1u << 1)` | The reader is gone. A writer's next write fails. |

## Enumerations

### `PipeRole` { #piperole }

Which end of a pipe a process holds.

| Name | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `PIPE_WRITER` | `1` | Produces bytes. Waits on the space bit, signals the data bit. |
| `PIPE_READER` | `2` | Consumes bytes. Waits on the data bit, signals the space bit. |

## Structures

### `PipeCtl` { #pipectl }

Control words that travel with a ring: closed flags and the terminal's signals.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `flags` | `volatile uint32_t` | PIPE_F_*. |
| `dropped` | `volatile uint32_t` | PipeTryWriteAll() calls that found no room. |
| `eof_seq` | `volatile uint32_t` | Bumped by a terminal for each ^D; 0 for a plain pipe. |
| `eof_ack` | `volatile uint32_t` | Last eof_seq the reader has handled. |
| `eof_pos` | `volatile uint32_t` | Ring position the EOF applies at. |
| `intr_seq` | `volatile uint32_t` | Bumped by a terminal for each ^C; 0 for a plain pipe. |

### `PipeShm` { #pipeshm }

The header at the start of the shared page.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ring` | `ShmRingHdr` | The byte ring; size is a power of two. |
| `ctl` | [`PipeCtl`](#pipectl) | Closed flags and terminal signals. |

### `PipeEnd` { #pipeend }

One end of a pipe, as a space holds it. A plain pipe owns a page and shares one event between its two ends. A view (PipeViewInit()) borrows a ring somebody else owns, such as a terminal session's, and waits on its own event while kicking the peer's.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ring` | `ShmRingHdr *` | The ring's indices; NULL once the end is closed. |
| `ctl` | [`PipeCtl`](#pipectl) * | Its control words. |
| `data` | `uint8_t *` | The ring's data area. |
| `size` | `size_t` | Ring size in bytes, a power of two. |
| `shm` | [`PipeShm`](#pipeshm) * | The mapped page when this end owns one, else NULL. |
| `mem` | [`Handle`](../../types.md#handle) | The page's memory object, or -1 for a view. |
| `event` | [`Handle`](../../types.md#handle) | Event this end waits on. |
| `wait_mask` | [`EventWord`](../../types.md#eventword) | Bits of `event` that mean "something changed for me". |
| `kick` | [`Handle`](../../types.md#handle) | Event the peer waits on; the same as `event` for a plain pipe. |
| `kick_mask` | [`EventWord`](../../types.md#eventword) | Bits to signal after reading or writing. |
| `close_mask` | [`EventWord`](../../types.md#eventword) | Bits to signal when this end closes, so a waiting peer wakes. |
| `intr_seen` | `uint32_t` | Last ctl->intr_seq this end has reported. |
| `role` | [`PipeRole`](#piperole) | Which end this is. |

## Functions

### `CreatePipe` { #createpipe }

```c
Err CreatePipe(size_t size, PipeEnd *w, PipeEnd *r);
```

Makes a pipe and both of its ends, sharing one new event.

| Parameter | Direction | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `size` | in | Ring size in bytes: a power of two from PIPE_SIZE_MIN to PIPE_SIZE_MAX. |
| `w` | out | The writer end. |
| `r` | out | The reader end. |

**Returns:** ZUZU_OK, ERR_BADARG for a bad `size`, or ERR_NOMEM.

### `OpenPipe` { #openpipe }

```c
Err OpenPipe(PipeEnd *e, PipeRole role, Handle mem, Handle event, size_t data_bit, size_t space_bit);
```

Builds an end from handles the space was granted or received.

Maps `mem` and reads the ring size from the page. Takes ownership of both handles: PipeClose() closes them.

| Parameter | Direction | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `e` | out | The end. |
| `role` | in | PIPE_WRITER or PIPE_READER. |
| `mem` | in | The page, with PERM_MAP \| PERM_WRITE. |
| `event` | in | The event, with PERM_SEND, plus PERM_WAIT if this end ever blocks. |
| `data_bit` | in | Bit 0-30 for data. The event may be shared with other pipes. |
| `space_bit` | in | Bit 0-30 for space; ignored if this end never blocks. |

**Returns:** ZUZU_OK, ERR_BADARG, or the mapping error.

### `PipeDupHandles` { #pipeduphandles }

```c
Err PipeDupHandles(const PipeEnd *e, HandlePerms event_perms, Handle *mem, Handle *event);
```

Duplicates an end's handles so they can be granted to another space.

| Parameter | Direction | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `e` | in | The end to share. |
| `event_perms` | in | Rights for the event copy: PERM_SEND alone for an untrusted peer, plus PERM_WAIT for a trusted one. |
| `mem` | out | Receives the page copy (PERM_MAP \| PERM_WRITE \| PERM_TXFR). |
| `event` | out | Receives the event copy. |

**Returns:** ZUZU_OK, or the duplication error.

### `PipeWrite` { #pipewrite }

```c
int PipeWrite(PipeEnd *w, const void *buf, size_t len, Duration timeout);
```

Writes all `len` bytes, waiting for room.

| Parameter | Direction | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `w` | in | The writer. |
| `buf` | in | Bytes to send. |
| `len` | in | How many. |
| `timeout` | in | TIMEOUT_POLL, TIMEOUT_INFINITE, or milliseconds. |

**Returns:** Bytes written; fewer than `len` on timeout. A negative [Err](../../errors.md#err) if nothing was written: ERR_DEAD if the reader closed (a broken pipe), ERR_TIMEOUT, or ERR_INTR if a terminal raised ^C while waiting.

### `PipeTryWriteAll` { #pipetrywriteall }

```c
Err PipeTryWriteAll(PipeEnd *w, const void *buf, size_t len);
```

Writes all `len` bytes or none, and never blocks.

For loggers.

| Parameter | Direction | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `w` | in | The writer. |
| `buf` | in | Bytes to send. |
| `len` | in | How many. |

**Returns:** ZUZU_OK, ERR_BUFFULL (counted in PipeDropped()), or ERR_DEAD if the reader closed.

### `PipeRead` { #piperead }

```c
int PipeRead(PipeEnd *r, void *buf, size_t cap, Duration timeout);
```

Reads up to `cap` bytes, waiting for the first one.

| Parameter | Direction | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `r` | in | The reader. |
| `buf` | out | Where to store the bytes. |
| `cap` | in | Room in `buf`. |
| `timeout` | in | TIMEOUT_POLL, TIMEOUT_INFINITE, or milliseconds. |

**Returns:** Bytes read; 0 at EOF (writer closed and the ring is empty, or a terminal's ^D); ERR_TIMEOUT if nothing arrived in time; ERR_INTR if a terminal raised ^C while waiting.

### `PipeViewInit` { #pipeviewinit }

```c
void PipeViewInit(PipeEnd *e, PipeRole role, ShmRingHdr *ring, PipeCtl *ctl, uint8_t *data, size_t size, Handle event, EventWord wait_mask, Handle kick, EventWord kick_mask);
```

Makes an end over a ring that somebody else owns, such as a terminal session's.

Nothing is mapped or closed: ClosePipe() and PipeDetach() only forget the end.

| Parameter | Direction | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `e` | out | The end. |
| `role` | in | PIPE_WRITER or PIPE_READER. |
| `ring` | in | The ring's indices. |
| `ctl` | in | Its control words. |
| `data` | in | Its data area. |
| `size` | in | Ring size in bytes, a power of two. |
| `event` | in | Event this end waits on. |
| `wait_mask` | in | Bits of `event` that mean something changed for this end. |
| `kick` | in | Event to signal after reading or writing, and on close. |
| `kick_mask` | in | Bits to signal on `kick`. |

### `PipeDetach` { #pipedetach }

```c
void PipeDetach(PipeEnd *e);
```

Lets go of this end without marking it closed: unmaps and closes the handles only.

For a space that keeps a pipe's handles on behalf of another, so the peer is not told the end is gone. Use PipeMarkClosed() to tell it.

| Parameter | Direction | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `e` | in | The end; left unusable. |

### `ClosePipe` { #closepipe }

```c
void ClosePipe(PipeEnd *e);
```

Closes this end by setting its closed flag, waking the peer, unmapping and closing the handles.

| Parameter | Direction | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `e` | in | The end; left unusable. |
